description: A two-panel composite figure making one thermodynamic argument. (a) is the iron–carbon equilibrium phase diagram: x-axis "C content (wt.%)" from 0.0 to 1.5 (ticks 0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9, 1.2, 1.5); y-axis "Temperature (°C)" from about 600 to above 1400 (ticks 600, 800, 1000, 1200, 1400). Five fields are labelled: BCC (top-left, arrow pointing into it), FCC (broad right field), BCC+FCC (middle band), BCC+FCC+θ (small field near 1.1 wt.% C, arrow pointing into it) and BCC+Carbides (base field below two near-horizontal boundaries at roughly 700–770 °C). A vertical dashed line lies between the 0.3 and 0.6 wt.% C ticks; no numeric value is printed for it or for the horizontal boundaries. (b) plots "Fraction of phase" (0.0–1.0) against "Temperature (°C)" (about 500–1200) for a fixed composition, legend: Carbides (dark grey, near-flat ~0.06 then falling to zero at ~710 °C); BCC (red, ~0.94 at low temperature, steep drop, decreasing to a minimum ~0.33 near 1050 °C then slight rise); FCC (blue, zero until ~710 °C, rising to a peak ~0.66 near 1000–1050 °C). Together they show the carbide field vanishes below about 750 °C, the basis for the carbide/ferrite composite lamellae retained at low rolling temperature.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an Fe–C equilibrium phase diagram with axes C content (wt.%) 0.0–1.5 and Temperature (°C) spanning about 600 to above 1400, containing five labelled fields: BCC, FCC, BCC+FCC, BCC+FCC+θ and BCC+Carbides.
In (a) two near-horizontal boundary lines at roughly 700–770 °C separate the BCC+Carbides field below from the BCC+FCC field above; no temperature values are printed on these lines.
In (a) a vertical dashed line is drawn between the 0.3 and 0.6 wt.% C axis ticks; its numeric composition is not printed.
Panel (b) plots Fraction of phase (0.0–1.0) versus Temperature (°C) from about 500 to 1200 with the legend Carbides, BCC and FCC.
In (b) the Carbides curve is nearly flat at a small fraction at low temperature and falls to zero at about 710 °C.
In (b) the BCC curve is at about 0.94 at low temperature, drops sharply near 710 °C, decreases to a minimum near 0.33 around 1050 °C and then rises slightly toward 1200 °C.
In (b) the FCC curve is at zero until about 710 °C, rises steeply to about 0.32, peaks near 0.66 around 1000–1050 °C and then decreases slightly.
In (b) the BCC and FCC curves intersect at a phase fraction of about 0.5 between the 850 and 950 °C gridlines.
The caption states that (a) is the iron–carbon equilibrium phase diagram and (b) shows the volume fraction proportion of each phase.
The citing text states that the carbide stability temperature range below 750 °C was predicted by thermodynamic calculations (Fig. 6a).

The citing text states that as rolling temperature increases from 650 °C to 750 °C the proportion of carbide/ferrite composite lamellae decreases from 51.5 % to 43.3 %, consistent with the carbide stability range predicted in Fig. 6a.

The citing text states that according to the phase diagram (Fig. 6) carbides exist in the material of the low-temperature rolling zone, where they appear as ultra-fine spheres in the ferrite/carbide composite lamellae.

Phase-fraction vs temperature plot, x-axis Temperature (°C) ~500–1200, y-axis Fraction of phase 0.0–1.0; three curves labelled Carbides (dark), BCC (red) and FCC (blue). Carbides drop to zero at ~710 °C, BCC falls from ~0.94 to a minimum ~0.33 near 1050 °C, FCC rises from zero at ~710 °C to a peak ~0.66 near 1000–1050 °C; BCC and FCC cross near 0.5 fraction between the 850 and 950 °C gridlines.
